# Anāthapiṇḍikovāda Sutta (MN 143 (PTS MN iii 258))
**ID:** MN 143 (PTS MN iii 258)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Anāthapiṇḍikovāda Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** Advice to Anāthapiṇḍika
**PTS:** MN iii 258

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Anāthapiṇḍikovāda Sutta* ("Advice to Anāthapiṇḍika", MN 143) is the 143rd discourse of the *Majjhimanikāya*, situated within the *Saḷāyatanavagga* [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995; SuttaCentral]. Set at Jeta's Grove near Sāvatthī, the narrative centers on the terminal illness and demise of the Buddha's foremost lay patron, Anāthapiṇḍika [SuttaCentral; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995; Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. Facing severe pain on his deathbed, Anāthapiṇḍika sends a messenger requesting the Venerable Sāriputta to visit him out of compassion [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995; Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. Accompanied by Ānanda, Sāriputta delivers a penetrating sermon on total non-attachment, systematically admonishing the dying householder not to cling to the six internal sense bases, six external sense objects, six classes of sensory consciousness, six sense contacts, and six feelings, as well as the elements, the five aggregates, the immaterial attainments, and this world or the next [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Buswell & Lopez 2014; Anālayo 2014]. Moved by instructions of a depth rarely imparted to householders, Anāthapiṇḍika weeps [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Galasek 2016; Anālayo 2016]. Following his death, he is reborn in the Tusita heaven and appears that night before the Buddha as a radiant deva praising Sāriputta and the Dhamma, an encounter later related and confirmed to Ānanda [Humphreys 1956; Bodhi 2003; Flores 2008; Freedman 1977; Thanissaro 2013].
Curated parallels recorded by SuttaCentral include versions across the Chinese Āgamas—Madhyama-āgama (MĀ 28), Saṁyukta-āgama (SĀ 1032, SĀ 593; SĀ² 187 / T 100), and Ekottarika-āgama (EĀ 51.8)—as well as a Sanskrit fragment (SHT sutta 66) [SuttaCentral; Anālayo 2014; Anālayo 2016; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. In the Pali Canon, close textual and verse parallels recur in the *Sotāpatti Saṁyutta* (SN 55.26), *Devatā Saṁyutta* (SN 1.48), and *Devaputta Saṁyutta* (SN 2.20) [SuttaCentral; Bodhi 2003]. DharmaNexus matches confirm these relations: Sāriputta's instruction shares extensive prose with SN 55.26 (§2.14–4.1), while the posthumous verses match SN 1.48 (§17.2–17.18) and SN 2.20 (§17.1–20.6) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the teaching on sensory non-clinging with the *Channovāda Sutta* (MN 144) and *Dhanañjāni Sutta* (MN 97), and establishes cross-language alignments with the Chinese Āgama parallels in T 26, T 99, T 100, and T 125 [DharmaNexus]. The sutta is additionally cited in the *Nettippakaraṇa* [SuttaCentral].
